newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa plans gradual sale of stockpiled crude oil.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa plans gradual sale of stockpiled crude oil.

text.p: South Africa would manage a planned 12 million barrel reduction of its strategic oil stockpile in a way that did not affect the market, Minerals and Energy Affairs director-general Gert Venter said on Wednesday.
"It is a thing that we will manage down gradually. We will not suddenly dump a lot of oil on the market," he told Reuters.

Minerals and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna earlier announced at a news briefing that the Cabinet had decided to reduce the government's 48 million barrel stockpile of oil to 36 million barrels, or 90 days' supply.

He said the stockpile, kept at storage tanks at Saldanha Bay and in disused mines inland, was not in line with international norms and it was strategically no longer necessary to hold such high levels.
The proceeds of the sale, which could raise up to $240 million, would go to the Treasury.

Venter said the crude was of good quality. "We have been buying Iranian light for a long time and this would be good quality and we will sell at the best price that we can get for it. Ideally, one would prefer to sell it locally."
He could not say when the sell-off would start as the Strategic Fuel Fund, which manages stockpiles, had only just been informed of Cabinet's decision.
Asked how the oil would be sold, Venter said that depended "on the way we manage it and where we get the best price.
"Sometimes contract is better in a declining market but in a growing market, spot is actually better," he said.
Venter said that the government had been gradually reducing its oil stockpile over the last two years.
"The important thing is not the volume that we put on the market but the fact that we are loosening up assets in the sense that you are getting money in to do other things with it," Venter said.
